subject: Physics
title: Error combination
concept: Relative errors add when quantities multiply or divide. A power becomes a multiplier.
q: For Z = A^2 / C^3, the maximum relative error is
easy: Powers become multipliers. A negative power still adds in the maximum error.

subject: Physics
title: Vernier and screw gauge
concept: Least count is the smallest change the instrument can show. A zero error must be added or subtracted before the reading is used.
q: A positive zero error on a screw gauge means
options: The true reading is less than the observed reading
easy: A positive zero error means the instrument already reads above zero when the gap is closed.

subject: Physics
title: Variable acceleration
concept: If acceleration depends on velocity or position, the constant-acceleration formulas are out. Use a = v dv/dx or a = dv/dt and separate.
q: Acceleration is given as a function of velocity. The first step is
options: Separate variables. Do not use v = u + at
easy: Constant-acceleration formulas need constant a.

subject: Physics
title: Projectile on an incline
concept: On level ground, horizontal velocity is constant. On an incline, take axes along and perpendicular to the incline.
q: Time to the top of a level-ground projectile is
easy: Vertical velocity falls from u sinθ to zero at rate g.

subject: Physics
title: Constraint and friction
concept: Net force sets the acceleration. A string constraint links the accelerations. Static friction adjusts up to μs N.
q: Two blocks move together only if
options: Required friction is within the maximum static friction
easy: One acceleration needs enough friction, up to μN.

subject: Physics
title: Work-energy and potential
concept: Work by a variable force is the integral of F dx. For a conservative force, F = -dU/dx. A minimum of U is stable.
q: Stable equilibrium on a U-x curve is
easy: A minimum pushes the body back.

subject: Physics
title: Cavity and restitution
concept: A cavity is negative mass. The coefficient of restitution is relative speed of separation over relative speed of approach.
q: A hole cut from a disc moves the centre of mass
easy: Missing mass is negative mass.

subject: Physics
title: Pure rolling
concept: Torque is r cross F. Pure rolling on a fixed surface means the contact point is at rest, so v = Rω.
q: The no-slip condition on a fixed surface is
easy: Contact point at rest means v = Rω.

subject: Physics
title: Field inside a sphere
concept: Outside a sphere the field is like a point mass. Inside a uniform sphere the field is proportional to r.
q: Field inside a uniform solid sphere is
easy: Only the mass inside r pulls.

subject: Physics
title: Bernoulli and capillary
concept: Along a streamline, pressure, speed and height trade off. A small hole at depth h has efflux speed sqrt(2gh).
q: Efflux speed from a hole at depth h is
easy: The height drop becomes speed.

subject: Physics
title: Spring networks
concept: SHM means acceleration is minus a constant times displacement. Series springs add extensions, so the combination is softer.
q: Two equal springs in series have effective k
easy: Series springs share the force and add extensions.

subject: Physics
title: First law paths
concept: ΔU = Q + W with one sign convention. For an ideal gas, U depends only on temperature. Adiabatic means Q = 0.
q: Free expansion of an ideal gas into vacuum has
easy: No heat and no external work, so U and T stay.

subject: Physics
title: Beats and Doppler
concept: Beat frequency is the difference of two close frequencies. Doppler shifts the frequency when source or observer moves.
q: Beat frequency is
options: The difference of the two frequencies
easy: You hear the difference.

subject: Physics
title: Gauss
concept: Gauss's law is useful when symmetry makes E constant on a surface: sphere, long wire, infinite sheet.
q: Gauss is the fast tool for
options: A long wire or an infinite sheet
A dipole at a random point
easy: You need a surface where E is constant or zero.

subject: Physics
title: Dielectric and RC
concept: If the battery stays connected, voltage is fixed. Inserting a dielectric raises capacitance, so charge rises. The RC time constant is RC.
q: A battery stays connected as a dielectric is inserted. What rises?
easy: Voltage is fixed. Capacitance rises, so charge rises.

subject: Physics
title: Power and potentiometer
concept: Maximum power to a load from a cell is when load resistance equals internal resistance. A potentiometer reads at null deflection.
q: Maximum power to the load when internal resistance is r occurs at
easy: P = I squared R, and I = E/(R+r). The peak is at R = r.

subject: Physics
title: Helix
concept: A charge with velocity perpendicular to B moves in a circle of radius mv/(qB). A parallel component makes a helix.
q: The cyclotron radius is
easy: Magnetic force supplies the centripetal force.

subject: Physics
title: Motional emf
concept: Induced emf equals minus the rate of change of flux. A rod sliding on rails in a uniform B has emf B l v.
q: A rod sliding on rails in a uniform B has emf
easy: Area changes, so flux changes.

subject: Physics
title: Resonance
concept: In a series LCR circuit, voltage and current are in phase at resonance. Impedance is then just R.
q: At resonance in series LCR
easy: The reactances cancel.

subject: Physics
title: Lens and prism
concept: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f. An object at the focus of a convex lens gives an image at infinity. A prism has minimum deviation at symmetric passage.
q: Object at the focus of a convex lens. The image is
easy: Rays from the focus leave parallel.

subject: Physics
title: Fringe width
concept: In Young's experiment, fringe width is λD/d. A thin sheet in one path shifts the central fringe.
q: If slit separation d increases, fringe width
easy: β is inversely proportional to d.

subject: Physics
title: Photoelectric
concept: K_max = hν - φ. Below the threshold frequency, no electrons leave, however bright the light.
q: Stopping potential depends on
easy: Intensity changes the number of electrons, not the energy of each.

subject: Physics
title: Levels and decay
concept: The photon energy is the difference of two levels. After one half-life, the number of undecayed nuclei is half.
q: After one half-life, N is
easy: Half-life is the time to halve, whatever N is.

subject: Physics
title: Forward bias and gates
concept: A p-n junction conducts in forward bias, when the p side is at higher potential. NAND and NOR are universal gates.
q: In forward bias, the p side is
easy: Forward bias lowers the barrier.

subject: Chemistry
title: Limiting reagent
concept: The mole counts particles. The limiting reagent is the one that runs out first. Molarity changes with temperature because volume changes.
q: Molarity changes with temperature because
easy: Moles stay. Volume expands, so molarity falls.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nodes and Balmer
concept: Radial nodes are n - l - 1. A Balmer line ends at n = 2.
q: A Balmer line ends at
easy: Balmer ends at 2. Lyman ends at 1.

subject: Chemistry
title: Real gases
concept: Z = PV/nRT. Z less than 1 means attractive forces dominate. The van der Waals a corrects for attractions.
q: Z less than 1 means
easy: Attractions pull the pressure below the ideal value.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hess and Gibbs
concept: ΔH is heat at constant pressure. Hess's law says the change depends on start and end. ΔG less than 0 means spontaneous.
q: Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas has
easy: U depends only on T for an ideal gas.

subject: Chemistry
title: Buffer and Ksp
concept: K is fixed at a given temperature. A buffer resists pH change. Common ion lowers solubility.
q: A common ion on a weak acid
easy: The extra ion pushes the equilibrium back.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation number
concept: Oxidation is a rise in oxidation number. Reduction is a fall. Electrons lost equal electrons gained.
q: In a redox equation
easy: Count the electrons on both sides.

subject: Chemistry
title: Anomalies
concept: Ionisation energy generally rises across a period. N is above O because the half-filled p set is stable.
q: Ionisation energy of N is above O because
options: N has a half-filled p subshell
easy: The half-filled set is unusually stable.

subject: Chemistry
title: VSEPR and MOT
concept: Electron pairs stay as far apart as they can. A lone pair takes more room. Bond order is half the difference of bonding and antibonding electrons.
q: Water is bent because
easy: Four pairs, two of them lone, give a bent shape.

subject: Chemistry
title: Anomaly
concept: Lithium and beryllium differ from the rest of their groups because they are small and polarising.
q: Li differs from other alkali metals because
options: It is small and polarises anions
easy: Small size and high charge density.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diborane
concept: Diborane has two 3-centre-2-electron bonds. Graphite conducts in the plane because of delocalised electrons.
q: The banana bonds in diborane are
easy: Two electrons are shared by three atoms.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbocation and aromaticity
concept: A more stable carbocation is easier to form. Aromatic rings follow 4n+2 pi electrons and are planar and cyclic.
q: Usually the most stable is
easy: Alkyl groups stabilise the positive carbon.

subject: Chemistry
title: Optical
concept: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images. A meso compound has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive.
q: A meso compound is
options: Optically inactive because of internal symmetry
easy: The two halves cancel.

subject: Chemistry
title: Markovnikov
concept: Alkenes add HX by Markovnikov unless peroxide is present for HBr. Ozonolysis cuts the double bond.
q: Peroxide changes the addition of
easy: Only HBr has a useful peroxide path.

subject: Chemistry
title: Colligative
concept: A colligative property depends on the number of particles. The van't Hoff factor counts association or dissociation.
q: i is less than 1 when
options: The solution is forced to i = 1
easy: Association means fewer particles.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nernst
concept: Oxidation is on the left, reduction on the right. At 298 K, E = E° - (0.059/n) log Q.

subject: Chemistry
title: Order and half-life
concept: Order is experimental. A first-order half-life does not depend on concentration. Nuclear decay is first order.
q: A first-order half-life is 10 min. After 20 min the reactant is
easy: Two half-lives leave one quarter.

subject: Chemistry
title: Packing and adsorption
concept: A void surrounded by six spheres is octahedral. Langmuir assumes a monolayer with no interaction between adsorbed molecules.
q: A void surrounded by six spheres is
easy: Six neighbours make an octahedral hole.

subject: Chemistry
title: CFT
concept: Coordination number counts donor atoms. A strong-field ligand pairs electrons and gives low spin in an octahedral complex.
q: A strong-field octahedral ligand gives
easy: A large split makes pairing cheaper.

subject: Chemistry
title: Colour
concept: Transition-metal colour often comes from d-d transitions. A vacant or full d set usually has no d-d colour.
q: A vacant or full d set usually means
easy: A d-d jump needs a partly filled d set.

subject: Chemistry
title: Xenon fluorides
concept: XeF2 is linear. XeF4 is square planar. Count the electron pairs, then place the lone pairs.
q: XeF2 is
easy: Five pairs, three of them lone, give a linear molecule.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group separation
concept: Cations are separated by group reagents. Group II precipitates as sulphides in acidic H2S. Group IV precipitates as sulphides in basic H2S.
q: Group II sulphides precipitate in
easy: Low sulphide concentration in acid precipitates only the less soluble sulphides.

subject: Chemistry
title: SN1 and SN2
concept: SN2 inverts the carbon and is faster on a less hindered carbon. SN1 makes a carbocation.
q: SN2 is fastest on
easy: The nucleophile needs room.

subject: Chemistry
title: Phenol acidity
concept: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised.
q: Phenol is acidic because
options: The phenoxide ion spreads the charge
easy: The anion is stabilised by the ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aldol
concept: A nucleophile attacks the carbonyl carbon. An aldol needs an alpha hydrogen on the enolate partner.
q: A carbonyl with no alpha hydrogen cannot
options: Form an enolate for an aldol
easy: No alpha hydrogen means no enolate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acyl reactivity
concept: Acid chlorides are the most reactive acyl derivatives. Amides are the least.
q: The most reactive acyl derivative is usually
easy: The chloride leaves easily.

subject: Chemistry
title: Basicity
concept: In water, solvation and steric effects change the gas-phase order. Aniline is a weaker base because the lone pair is delocalised into the ring.
q: Aniline is a weaker base than ethylamine because
options: The lone pair is delocalised into the ring
easy: The lone pair is shared with the ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reducing sugar
concept: A reducing sugar has a free hemiacetal. Sucrose does not, because both anomeric carbons are tied.
q: Sucrose is non-reducing because
easy: The anomeric carbons are locked.

subject: Mathematics
title: Domain
concept: The domain is the set of inputs that keep the expression defined. A square root needs a non-negative inside.
q: The domain of sqrt(x-2) is
easy: The inside of the root must be at least zero.

subject: Mathematics
title: Location of roots
concept: Both roots are greater than k if the sum and product conditions hold and the vertex is on the right side of k, with f(k) positive for an upward parabola.
q: For an upward parabola, both roots greater than k needs
options: f(k) > 0, vertex to the right of k, and sum of roots positive relative to k
easy: The graph must sit above the axis at k and cross later.

subject: Mathematics
title: Modulus
concept: A complex number is a point. The modulus is the distance from the origin. |z1 z2| = |z1| |z2|.

subject: Mathematics
title: AM-GM
concept: An AP has a constant difference. A GP has a constant ratio. For positive numbers, AM is at least GM.
q: AM - GM for positive numbers is
easy: Equality when the numbers are equal.

subject: Mathematics
title: Order
concept: A permutation arranges. A combination selects. Order matters only in the first.
q: Ways to choose 2 from 5

subject: Mathematics
title: General term
concept: The general term of (a+b)^n is C(n,r) a^(n-r) b^r. The index r starts at 0.
q: The term with b^r has coefficient
easy: Pick r factors of b and the rest a.

subject: Mathematics
title: General solution
concept: One angle is not the full solution. Add the period.
q: sin x = 1/2 needs
options: The principal angles plus the period
easy: The wave repeats.

subject: Mathematics
title: Family of lines
concept: Parallel lines have equal slopes. The family through the intersection of L1 = 0 and L2 = 0 is L1 + λ L2 = 0.
q: Parallel lines have
easy: Same slope means same direction.

subject: Mathematics
title: Chord of contact
concept: From an external point, the chord of contact is the line joining the points of tangency. Its equation comes from T = 0.
q: The chord of contact from an external point is
options: The line joining the two points of tangency
easy: It joins the touch points.

subject: Mathematics
title: Parabola focus
concept: A parabola is equidistant from a focus and a directrix. For y^2 = 4ax the focus is (a, 0).
q: Focus of y^2 = 4ax is
easy: The focus is a units from the vertex.

subject: Mathematics
title: Standard limit
concept: A limit is the value approached. Plug-in is not allowed when it gives 0/0.
q: lim x→0 sin x / x is
easy: This standard limit is 1.

subject: Mathematics
title: Bijective
concept: One-one and onto together make a bijection. Only then is there an inverse function.
q: A function has an inverse only if it is
easy: Both conditions are needed.

subject: Mathematics
title: Principal value
concept: Each inverse trig function has one principal branch. arcsin returns an angle in [-π/2, π/2].
q: The principal value of arcsin is in
easy: arcsin returns an angle in that closed interval.

subject: Mathematics
title: Corner
concept: Continuity means the limit equals the value. A corner can be continuous and still not differentiable.
q: |x| at 0 is
easy: The graph is joined. The slope jumps.

subject: Mathematics
title: Increasing
concept: f' > 0 on an interval means f is increasing there. A local maximum on an open interval has f' = 0 and a change from rising to falling.
q: If f'(x) > 0 on an interval, f is
easy: Positive slope means the value rises.

subject: Mathematics
title: Parts
concept: Integration by parts uses ∫ u dv = uv - ∫ v du. Choose u by the ILATE order.
q: The derivative of an indefinite integral of f is
easy: They undo each other.

subject: Mathematics
title: King
concept: King's property replaces x by a+b-x. It is the usual tool when the integrand has f(x) and f(a+b-x).
q: King's property replaces x by
easy: The interval is flipped onto itself.

subject: Mathematics
title: Between curves
concept: The area between two curves is the integral of the upper minus the lower, between the intersection points.
q: Area between curves uses
easy: Subtract the lower from the upper.

subject: Mathematics
title: Integrating factor
concept: dy/dx + P y = Q is solved by multiplying by e to the integral of P.
q: The integrating factor is
easy: It makes the left side a product rule.

subject: Mathematics
title: Singular
concept: Matrix multiplication is not commutative. A zero determinant means no inverse.
q: If det A = 0, AX = B
easy: No inverse means not one unique solution.

subject: Mathematics
title: Dot and cross
concept: The dot product is a scalar. The cross product is a vector perpendicular to both. The scalar triple product is the volume of the parallelepiped.
q: a · b = 0 means
options: They are perpendicular, if neither is zero
easy: Zero dot product means a right angle.

subject: Mathematics
title: Skew lines
concept: A line needs a point and a direction. Skew lines do not meet and are not parallel. Their shortest distance is along the common perpendicular.
q: Skew lines
options: Do not meet and are not parallel
easy: If they were coplanar and did not meet, they would be parallel.

subject: Mathematics
title: Bayes
concept: Conditional probability is the chance given that something already happened. Bayes updates a prior with evidence.
q: P(A|B) is
easy: Condition on B, so divide by P(B).
